To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the antiviral crisis is regulated by a single molecule, (2) the antivirals crisis is regulated by the antiviral molecule, (3) the antivirus molecule regulates all the antiviruses, (4) the antiviras molecule is regulated by all the antiviral molecules, (5) the antivira molecule is regulated by the virus, (6) the virus is regulated by the viral molecule,

(i) a single antiviral molecule, the antiviral RNA-binding protein RBP1 (ii) is sufficient to induce a strong antiviral state (iii) that protects against a wide range of unrelated viruses (iv) and that this effect is mediated by the induction of a set of antiviral genes (v) whose expression is dependent on the antiviral factor IRF3.

(i) the antiviral response in the host is a complex process that involves a number of signaling pathways and (ii) the host response to viral infection is regulated by one molecule (NF-κB) which regulates a number of other signaling molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the antiviral state and its induction by interferons.
the molecular basis of antiviral defense.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms of antiviral innate immune responses and the development of novel antiviral drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the context of antiviral response, IRF3 and IRF7 are two major transcription factors that play a critical role in the regulation of type I IFN genes and IFN-stimulated genes, and that the regulation of type III IFN genes by IRF7 is a novel finding.
, in the absence of a specific virus, the innate immune system is not activated.

, although the virus-host interaction is a complex process involving multiple factors, the antiviral response of the host is a coordinated process that involves multiple signaling pathways, and the regulation of each of these pathways is a complex and multifaceted process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered the molecular mechanism for the regulation of the innate immunity in the fruit fly D. melanogaster.
we are trying to understand the molecular mechanism behind how antiviral crisis is induced.
the antiviral response is regulated at many levels and by many molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a single target molecule that regulates the antiviral crisis in plants.
there is a common molecular mechanism that regulates the antiviral state in different tissues and in different viral infection models.
we can now identify a single molecule that regulates the entire antiviral response.
